contentObjective: I can determine the mean of a data set, use a target mean to find a missing value, and explain the mean as the fair share and the balance point of the data.
languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words mean, average, measure of center, balance point, and data set.

vocabulary.definition: The average of a data set. Add all the values, then divide by how many values there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El promedio de un conjunto de datos. Suma todos los valores y divide entre cuántos valores hay.
vocabulary.visual: Miguel earned $60 in 4 days: 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so the mean is $15 per day.
vocabulary.cloze: The value found by adding all the data and dividing by how many values there are is the ___.

examples.why: Add the values, then divide by how many there are.
That is the total; the mean still needs the division.

vocabulary.definition: Another word for the mean — the amount each value would be if the total were shared equally.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Otra palabra para la media: la cantidad que tendría cada valor si el total se repartiera en partes iguales.
vocabulary.visual: A player averages 15 points per game, so over 10 games she scores 15 × 10 = 150 points in all.
vocabulary.cloze: A common everyday word that means the same thing as the mean is the ___.

examples.why: That is the total before sharing.

vocabulary.definition: A single number used to describe the middle, or typical value, of a whole data set.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo número que se usa para describir el centro, o valor típico, de todo un conjunto de datos.
vocabulary.visual: The mean, $15, is one measure of center that describes all four of Miguel's days at once.
vocabulary.cloze: A single number that describes the typical value of a whole data set is a ___.

examples.why: One number standing for the typical value.

vocabulary.definition: The value where the total distance of the data above it equals the total distance below it. The mean is the balance point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El valor donde la distancia total de los datos por encima es igual a la distancia total por debajo. La media es el punto de equilibrio.
vocabulary.visual: With a target mean of 15, points totaling 13 below must be matched by points totaling 13 above.
vocabulary.cloze: The value where the total amount above equals the total amount below is the ___.

examples.why: Distances above and below it cancel out.
Everything sits below it, so nothing balances.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Honor Roll
revealWordProblem.text:
Shanice wants to be on the honor roll for the next marking period. She works out that her mean test score has to be at least 90 in both math and science. Her test scores so far this grading period are shown in her student portal.
Question: How likely is it that Shanice will make the honor roll? Explain what she still has to do.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A student portal screen showing recent test scores: math scores 88, 82, 92, and 95, and science scores 95, 85, and 88.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Math so far: 88 + 82 + 92 + 95 = 357, a mean of 89.25. With one more test the mean is (357 + x) ÷ 5, and that is at least 90 when 357 + x ≥ 450, so x ≥ 93. Science so far: 95 + 85 + 88 = 268, a mean of about 89.3. With one more test the mean is (268 + x) ÷ 4, and that is at least 90 when 268 + x ≥ 360, so x ≥ 92. Shanice needs at least 93 in math and 92 in science. She has already scored 92 and 95 in math and 95 in science, so it is possible — but she has no room to slip.

questions.explanation: Add the values: 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 = 28. There are 4 values, so the mean is 28 ÷ 4 = 7.
choiceFeedback: 6 is another value from the list; picking a value from the data is not the same as adding and dividing.
8 is one of the values in the list, but the mean is the leveled amount for all four, found by dividing the total by 4.
28 is the total of the four values, not the mean — you still have to divide that total by 4.
hints: The mean is what each value would be if the total were shared out equally among all four numbers.
Mean = total ÷ how many values. Count first: there are 4 values here.
Step 1: add 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 to get the total. Step 2: divide that total by 4.

Media = total ÷ cuántos valores hay. Cuenta primero: aquí hay 4 valores.
Paso 1: suma 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 para obtener el total. Paso 2: divide ese total entre 4.

questions.stem: Miguel earned $60 walking dogs over 4 days. What is his mean daily earning?
questions.explanation: The total is $60 and there are 4 days, so the mean is 60 ÷ 4 = $15 per day.
choiceFeedback: $4 is the number of days, not an amount of money; the days are what you divide BY.
$20 comes from dividing 60 by 3 instead of 4 — count the days again.
$60 is the total for all 4 days combined — a typical single day must be much smaller than the whole week's total.
hints: A typical day is the amount Miguel would earn if he earned the SAME amount all 4 days.
You already know the total, so only one step is left: split that total equally among the days.
Divide the $60 total by the 4 days to find the equal share for one day.
questions.stemEs: Miguel ganó $60 paseando perros durante 4 días. ¿Cuál es su ganancia media diaria?
questions.explanationEs: El total es $60 y hay 4 días, así que la media es 60 ÷ 4 = $15 por día.
hintsEs: Un día típico es la cantidad que Miguel ganaría si ganara LO MISMO los 4 días.
Ya conoces el total, así que solo falta un paso: repartir ese total en partes iguales entre los días.
Divide el total de $60 entre los 4 días para hallar la parte igual de un día.

9 is the fourth value in the list, not the leveled value for all five numbers.
35 is the sum of the five values — the mean requires the second step of dividing that sum by 5.

hintsEs: Media significa promedio: nivela los cinco números para que todos sean iguales.

reviewHighlights.formula: Mean = (Sum of all values) ÷ (Total number of values)
steps: 1. Add all data values together to find the total sum
2. Divide the sum by the count of data values
3. Concept: The mean represents the fair share or balance point of the data
reviewHighlights.watchOut: The most common mistake with the mean is adding correctly and then dividing by the wrong number — or not dividing at all. Students report the total (for 8, 10, 6, 12 they say the mean is 36) or they divide by a count that does not match the data, such as dividing a 4-value total by 5, or skipping a zero when counting the values. Before you finish, do two things: count the values in the data set out loud, and check that your mean lands between the smallest and largest value. A mean of 36 for data that never goes above 12 is impossible.

level3.prompt: Sofia realized she made an error: she actually scored 12 points in Game 8, not 10. Her other games are unchanged (12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15, and 18). How does this change the number of points she needs in Game 10 to average 15 points per game? Show how you know.
level3.promptEs: Sofía se dio cuenta de un error: en realidad anotó 12 puntos en el Juego 8, no 10. Sus otros juegos no cambian (12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15 y 18). ¿Cómo cambia esto los puntos que necesita en el Juego 10 para promediar 15 puntos por juego? Muestra cómo lo sabes.
level3.sentenceFrame: Her new total after 9 games is ___ points. To average 15 over 10 games she still needs ___ points in all, so Game 10 must now be ___ points. That is ___ points fewer than before, because ___.
hints: Only one value changed, so you do not have to re-add everything from scratch.
Decide first how much the 9-game total moved, then compare that new total to the 150 points she still needs.
The old 9-game total was 133 and Game 8 went up by 2. Update the total, then subtract it from 150.
hintsEs: Solo cambió un valor, así que no tienes que volver a sumar todo desde cero.
Decide primero cuánto se movió el total de 9 juegos y luego compara ese nuevo total con los 150 puntos que aún necesita.
El total anterior de 9 juegos era 133 y el Juego 8 subió 2. Actualiza el total y luego réstalo de 150.
level3.explanation: Raising Game 8 from 10 to 12 adds 2 points, so the 9-game total goes from 133 to 135. The target has not changed: a mean of 15 over 10 games still needs 15 × 10 = 150 points in all. So Game 10 must now supply 150 − 135 = 15 points instead of 17 — exactly 2 fewer, because every point gained earlier is a point she no longer has to score later.
level3.explanationEs: Subir el Juego 8 de 10 a 12 agrega 2 puntos, así que el total de 9 juegos pasa de 133 a 135. El objetivo no cambia: una media de 15 en 10 juegos sigue necesitando 15 × 10 = 150 puntos en total. Así que el Juego 10 debe aportar ahora 150 − 135 = 15 puntos en vez de 17, exactamente 2 menos, porque cada punto ganado antes es un punto que ya no tiene que anotar después.

level3.stem: A data set has a mean of 20. Every value in the data set is then increased by 4. What is the new mean?
level3.explanation: If every value moves up by 4, the balance point moves up by 4 as well, so the new mean is 20 + 4 = 24. In totals: adding 4 to each of n values adds 4n to the total, and 4n ÷ n = 4.
choiceFeedback: 5 comes from dividing 20 by 4; the change was an addition to each value, so the mean changes by addition too.
20 would be right only if the values did not move, but every single value shifted up by 4.
80 comes from multiplying the mean by 4, but the values were increased by 4, not multiplied by 4.
hints: Picture the mean as a balance point and every data value sliding 4 units to the right.
If the whole data set shifts by the same amount, does the center shift too, or stay put?
Try a tiny example: 18, 20, 22 has a mean of 20. Add 4 to each value and find the new mean.
level3.stemEs: Un conjunto de datos tiene una media de 20. Luego cada valor del conjunto aumenta en 4. ¿Cuál es la nueva media?
level3.explanationEs: Si cada valor sube 4, el punto de equilibrio también sube 4, así que la nueva media es 20 + 4 = 24. En totales: sumar 4 a cada uno de los n valores agrega 4n al total, y 4n ÷ n = 4.
hintsEs: Imagina la media como un punto de equilibrio y cada valor deslizándose 4 unidades a la derecha.
Si todo el conjunto se desplaza la misma cantidad, ¿el centro también se desplaza o se queda igual?
Prueba un ejemplo pequeño: 18, 20, 22 tiene media 20. Suma 4 a cada valor y halla la nueva media.

tool.title: Sofia's First 9 Games — One Dot per Game
tool.caption: Each dot is the points Sofia scored in one game. The nine dots total 133 points. A mean of 15 across 10 games needs 150 in all, so game 10 has to bring 17.
